business:
OZ
Vision Inc. (the “Company”) currently operates as a transportation and logistics company with the ability to deliver merchandise
and other items throughout the United States. The Company has had limited operations since its founding. On September 21, 2023, the Company
acquired certain assets of Jebour Two Limited held by its subsidiary Fighting Leagues LV (“Fighting Leagues”). The acquired
assets will allow the Company, should it determine to do so, to promote combat sports events and selling related media rights internationally.
The assets acquired include the Nevada State Athletic Commission Professional Promoter license. The Professional Promoter license is
unique, as it allows the Company in the state of Nevada to produce live Kickboxing, Boxing, and MMA shows. Additionally, the transaction
included Producers Lifetime rights for the 40 shows previously held by Fighting Leagues. These rights are worldwide and perpetual, encompassing
broadcast TV and production rights. Furthermore, the acquisition of the assets of Fighting Leagues also included production and stage
equipment. These assets allow the Company to have the necessary equipment for producing shows at any given time. As of the date of this
Report, we have not commenced any business operations that utilize the Fighting Leagues assets.
On
May 5, 2024, the Company amended its Articles of Incorporation with the Nevada Secretary of State to change its name from “United
Express Inc.” to “OZ Vision Inc.” FINRA’s Corporate Actions office approved the name change on September 23,
2025. Our common stock traded under the symbol “UNXP” through December 1, 2025 and has traded under the symbol “OZVN”
since December 2, 2025. During the transition period from May 5, 2024 to September 23, 2025, the Company conducted business under both
names.
Revenues
During
the years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, the Company had revenue of $46,930 and $54,232, respectively. Revenue to date has been dependent
upon the success of our transportation and logistics business. Revenue has primarily been from less than five customers and as such we
are dependent upon those customers. As a result of this concentration in revenues there is doubt about the stability of our ability to
generate revenues into the future.
We
offer a dispatch service and logistics services to our customers including parcel shipping services for single or multiple pallets of
freight to the destination requested by the customers.
Marketing
Program
The
Company does minimal marketing.
Industry
Background and Competition
The
transportation and logistics industry is fragmented with large national and regional carriers as well as smaller independent owner operators.
Typically, the transportation and logistics industry is segmented into three segments:
●
Private Fleet – shippers who own and operate
their own fleet to move their own goods.
●
Truckload – transport large shipments from origination
to destination of a complete load.
●
Less-Than-Load – carry numerous shipments from
multiple shippers to create a full load.
The
Company has limited resources and many of our competitors have more substantial resources than us. Our limited resources may limit our
ability to successfully compete.
Business
Strategy
We
provide management service for long and short distance logistics for clients in the Company’s target market areas. Additionally,
the Company has begun to explore strategic opportunities to promote, produce, and sponsor, live mixed martial arts fights. The Company
owns a Nevada Promoters License which allows the Company the ability to produce live mixed martial arts events in Nevada. Mixed martial
arts is one of the fastest growing sports in the United States. Live events can generate revenue through sponsorships, ticket sales,
broadcast rights, and other ancillary activities. Though the Company is exploring this strategic opportunity, there can be no assurances
that the Company will further pursue these opportunities or that, if pursued, any of these strategic opportunities will result in a successful
line of business for the Company. There is also the risk that as the Company evaluates these strategic opportunities that time and attention
will be diverted from the transportation and logistics operations.
Employees
Other
than our President, Chief Executive Officer and Director, Andrei Stoukan, we have no employees. All services to our customers are provided
by third party consultants or contractors.
Research
and Development
The
Company did not perform any research and development during fiscal years 2026 and 2025.
Fees
In
dispatch and logistics, we charge depending on working time and distance. In the selling process, we based on reasonable margin between
wholesale price and retail price. For the period from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2026, we generated revenues from our customers based
on the above principle.
Governmental
Regulation
We
are subject to federal, state, local regulations and other regulations applicable to our transportation business.
Available
Information
Currently
our common stock is listed on OTCID marketplace. We file annual reports, quarterly reports, and other information with the Securities
and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. The SEC maintains an internet website
at http://www.sec.gov where you can access copies of most of our SEC
risks:
An
investment in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below and the other
information in this Report before investing in our common stock. If any of the following risks occur, our business, operating results
and financial condition could be seriously harmed. Currently, shares of our common stock are publicly traded. The trading price of our
common stock could decline due to any of these risks, and you may lose all or part of your investment.
Risks
Related to Our Financial Condition and Liquidity
There
is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
At
June 30, 2026 we had $4,388 of cash, an accumulated deficit of $2,679,633 and negative working capital. As described in Note 10 to our
financial statements, these conditions raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern. Our financial statements
do not include any adjustments to the recoverability or classification of recorded assets, or to the amounts or classification of liabilities,
that might be necessary if we are unable to continue as a going concern. If we cannot continue as a going concern, you could lose your
entire investment.
We
will require additional financing, which may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.
Our
revenues are not sufficient to fund our operating costs, including the $40,000 to $70,000 of annual costs we expect to incur in operating
as a public reporting company. We have no commitments for additional capital and no credit facility. Any financing we do obtain may be
substantially dilutive to existing stockholders or may impose covenants that restrict our operations. If we are unable to raise capital
on acceptable terms, we will be required to curtail or cease operations.
Our
limited operating history and small revenue base make our results difficult to forecast, and we may never become profitable.
We
were formed on June 23, 2017 and have had limited operations since our founding. Our revenues were $46,930 for the year ended June 30,
2026 and $54,232 for the year ended June 30, 2025, and we recorded net losses of $58,671 and $65,601 in those periods. Because our expense
levels are based on our operating plans and our revenues are unpredictable, we may be unable to adjust spending in time to compensate
for a revenue shortfall.
We
depend on a small number of customers, and delays in customer payments can disrupt our operations.
Our
revenue has been derived from fewer than five customers in each of the last two fiscal years. The loss of any one of them would materially
reduce our revenues, and we may be unable to expand our customer base. Customers may take up to 30 days to pay for completed services,
and from time to time a broker withholds payment in whole or in part where there is a claimed delivery error. Because our expenses of
providing a service are incurred before we are paid, these delays can exceed our available cash and force us to suspend services temporarily.
We
depend on financial and other support from a significant stockholder, which we have no contractual right to receive.
At
June 30, 2026 we owed $1,042,647 to an entity owned and controlled by Mr. Orsat Zovko, a significant stockholder, arising from the acquisition
of our production and stage equipment. That obligation has no stated repayment terms. During the year ended June 30, 2026, a significant
stockholder also paid $19,000 of storage fees on our behalf, and we occupy our principal executive office free of charge under an informal
arrangement with a person described to us as a friend and business partner of Mr. Zovko. We have no written agreement entitling us to
any of this support. If the related party obligation were called for payment, or if the office arrangement or the payment of expenses
on our behalf were discontinued, we would not have the resources to satisfy the obligation or to replace the support, and our business
could fail.
Risks
Related to Our Business and Assets
We
have not commenced the combat sports business for which we acquired assets in 2023, and we may never do so.
In
September 2023 we acquired a State of Nevada professional promoter license, media rights to 40 previously produced shows, and production
and stage equipment. As of the date of this Report we have not commenced any business operations that use those assets, and we lack the
capital required to plan and hold live events. We have no operating history in combat sports promotion, and holding events requires significant
planning and capital, with any potential earnings not realized for a period of months after an event is committed. We may never commence
this line of business. If we do, we would face competition from established promoters with far greater resources, our results would depend
on consumer tastes that are unpredictable, and we would be exposed to liability for injuries to athletes that our insurance may not fully
cover. Time and attention devoted to evaluating this opportunity is diverted from our transportation and logistics operations.
Intangible
assets represent approximately 96% of our total assets, and an impairment would eliminate substantially all of our reported net assets.
Our
balance sheet at June 30, 2026 carried intangible assets of $13,098,890 against total assets of $13,713,695 and total stockholders’
equity of $12,509,178. The professional promoter license is treated as an indefinite-lived intangible asset, is not amortized, and is
tested for impairment using an income approach based on discounted cash flows. That valuation depends on projected revenues from a line
of business we have never operated, and is sensitive to the discount rate applied and the length of the forecast period. Our judgments
may prove incorrect. An impairment of this asset would materially reduce our reported total assets and stockholders’ equity and
could eliminate substantially all of our reported net assets, and would not be within our control to reverse.
Our
State of Nevada promoter license is subject to continuing regulatory requirements, and its lapse would adversely affect the value of
our principal asset.
We
hold a State of Nevada promoter license and are subject to the requirements of the State of Nevada and other regulatory agencies, which
require licenses for promoters, medical clearances and other permits for athletes and events. The license is the principal component
of the intangible asset described above. If we fail to comply with applicable regulations, or if the license lapses, is suspended or
is not renewed, we would be prohibited from promoting and conducting live events and the carrying value of our principal asset would
be adversely affected.
Our
production and stage equipment has never been placed in service, has been subject to theft, and continues to generate storage costs.
